# @motion-charts/core AI usage guide

Use this package when a React app needs beautiful animated charts for dashboards, ecommerce analytics, SaaS metrics, POS reports, admin panels, landing pages, or product UI.

Install:

npm install @motion-charts/core framer-motion

In Next.js App Router, render charts from a client component.

Best default pattern:

```tsx
"use client";

import { BarChart, ResponsiveChart } from "@motion-charts/core";

export function RevenueChart({ data }) {
  return (
    <ResponsiveChart minHeight={280} maxHeight={440}>
      {({ width, height }) => (
        <BarChart
          data={data}
          width={width}
          height={height}
          xKey="month"
          yKey="revenue"
          theme="aurora"
          animation={{ preset: "bouncy", stagger: 0.04 }}
          valueFormatter={(value) => `$${value.toLocaleString()}`}
          ariaLabel="Monthly revenue"
          showValues
        />
      )}
    </ResponsiveChart>
  );
}
```

Use cases:

- Ecommerce revenue by month: `BarChart`, theme `aurora` or `sunset`, show values.
- POS hourly sales trend: `Sparkline` in metric cards, theme `ocean`, animation `snappy`.
- SaaS users vs revenue: `MultiLineChart`, theme `midnight`, show legend and area.
- Acquisition channels: `DonutChart`, theme `candy`, show labels and center total.
- Inventory trend: `LineChart`, theme `minimal`, show area.

Theme names:

`aurora`, `midnight`, `candy`, `ocean`, `sunset`, `minimal`

Palette names:

`aurora`, `ocean`, `sunset`, `forest`, `candy`, `royal`, `fire`, `cyber`, `pastel`, `graphite`, `emerald`, `bloom`

Theme extension:

Pass `theme={{ base: "midnight", gridColor: "#334155" }}` to extend any named theme.

Zero inclusion / axis tuning:

- `yAxis={{ includeZero: false }}` (default for `LineChart` and `MultiLineChart` to maximize dynamic range)
- `yAxis={{ includeZero: true }}` (default for `BarChart`)

Animation presets:

`spring`, `gentle`, `snappy`, `bouncy`, `calm`, `dramatic`, `linear`
Exported helper: `animationPreset(presetName)`

Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 Level A):

Charts feature accessible roving `tabIndex={0}` on the active point/slice and `-1` on the rest, with arrow-key keyboard navigation (`ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Home`/`End`), visible high-contrast focus rings, and `aria-describedby` connected to live tooltips.

Prefer `ResponsiveChart` for real app pages. It supports CSS grid/flex layouts, opts into `min-width: 0`, ignores temporary zero-width observations, and clamps narrow-card margins so chart geometry stays inside the SVG viewport. For custom wrappers, add `style={{ minWidth: 0, width: "100%" }}`. Always pass `ariaLabel`. Use `valueFormatter` for money, percentages, compact numbers, and units. Date labels render as deterministic `YYYY-MM-DD` strings: UTC-midnight values such as `new Date("2026-03-01")` use UTC parts, while other Date values use local parts. Pass `dateFormatter` for an explicit timezone or instant policy. Use `colors={[...]}` when matching a brand system exactly.

Motion and rendering guidance:

- Data updates animate by default; `animation={{ initial: false }}` skips only the entrance and `animation={{ disabled: true }}` opts out of all motion.
- SSR renders final geometry. Do not add a client-only blank state to work around entrance animation.
- Reduced-motion users receive final geometry without animated transitions.
- Supply stable `id` values for `MultiLineChart.series` entries.
- For accessible charts, use a specific `ariaLabel`, keep a readable surface behind transparent chart SVGs, and test keyboard focus as well as pointer tooltips.

Common selection:

- Categorical comparison → `BarChart`
- Single time series → `LineChart`
- Multiple related time series → `MultiLineChart`
- Share of a whole → `DonutChart`
- Compact KPI trend → `Sparkline`
- Measured dashboard layout → `ResponsiveChart`
